body: State whether each disease is caused by a **virus**, **protist** or **bacterium**: herpes, typhoid fever, diphtheria, measles, leishmaniasis, malaria.
answer:
> [!answer]
> - Herpes: **virus**
> - Typhoid fever: **bacterium** (*Salmonella typhi*)
> - Diphtheria: **bacterium** (*Corynebacterium diphtheriae*)
> - Measles: **virus**
> - Leishmaniasis: **protist** (*Leishmania*)
> - Malaria: **protist** (*Plasmodium*)
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Antibiotics treat bacterial diseases, not viral ones.

## Simplified explanation

Viruses: herpes, measles; bacteria: typhoid, diphtheria; protists: leishmaniasis, malaria.

body: Define: (a) clade (b) taxon (c) viroid (d) prion.
answer:
> [!answer]
> (a) **Clade**: a group of organisms consisting of a common ancestor and **all** its descendants (monophyletic group).
> (b) **Taxon**: any named group at any rank of classification (e.g. a species, genus, family).
> (c) **Viroid**: a small, circular, infectious **RNA** molecule with **no protein coat** that infects plants.
> (d) **Prion**: an infectious **misfolded protein** with no nucleic acid that causes other proteins to misfold (e.g. mad cow disease, CJD).
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Viroids and prions are 'subviral' infectious agents.

## Simplified explanation

Ancestor + all descendants; named group; naked RNA; infectious protein.

body: State **three** goals of taxonomy and **two** reasons why classifying organisms is important.
answer:
> [!answer]
> Goals: (1) **identify** and describe organisms; (2) **name** them (nomenclature); (3) **classify** them into groups showing relationships; (4) reconstruct **evolutionary relationships** (phylogeny).
>
> Importance: makes the huge diversity of life **manageable to study**; allows **universal communication** using standard names; shows **evolutionary relationships**; helps predict characteristics of related organisms.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Taxonomy = identification, nomenclature and classification.

## Simplified explanation

Identify, name, classify; organise and communicate.

body: Distinguish between the **hierarchical (Linnaean)** and **cladistic** classification systems.
answer:
> [!answer]
> **Hierarchical** classification groups organisms into nested ranks (kingdom → species) mainly by **overall similarity** of observable characteristics; groups need not reflect common ancestry.
>
> **Cladistics** groups organisms only by **shared derived characters (synapomorphies)** inherited from a common ancestor, producing **cladograms** of monophyletic groups (clades); ranks are less important.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Cladistics reflects evolutionary history explicitly.

## Simplified explanation

Similarity and ranks vs shared derived traits and ancestry.

body: Match each group with its characteristic: retroviruses, green algae, thermophilic bacteria, nitrifying bacteria, slime moulds, dinoflagellates, sarcodines, euglenids, multicellular (brown) algae, diatoms.
answer:
> [!answer]
> - Retroviruses → **reverse transcription**
> - Green algae → **cellulose cell wall**
> - Thermophilic bacteria → **inhabit extremely hot environments**
> - Nitrifying bacteria → **chemoautotrophism**
> - Slime moulds → **fruiting body**
> - Dinoflagellates → **bioluminescence**
> - Sarcodines → **pseudopodia**
> - Euglenids → **eye spot**
> - Multicellular algae → **holdfast**
> - Diatoms → **frustule** (silica shell)
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Each group's signature feature.

## Simplified explanation

Learn one defining feature per group.

body: Give the Orders of: (a) newts (b) pythons (c) koalas (d) duck-billed platypus.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Monotremes lay eggs; marsupials carry young in a pouch.

## Simplified explanation

Urodela, Squamata, Marsupialia, Monotremata.

body: (a) Name the common feeding method of urochordates and cephalochordates. (b) Name two jawless vertebrates. (c) Give one example of a poisonous lizard.
answer:
> [!answer]
> (a) **Filter (suspension) feeding** using the pharyngeal slits.
> (b) **Lampreys** and **hagfish**.
> (c) The **Gila monster** (*Heloderma suspectum*) or the Mexican beaded lizard.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Pharyngeal slits are a basic chordate feature used for feeding in protochordates.

## Simplified explanation

Filter feeding; lamprey and hagfish; Gila monster.

body: Explain why the family **Boidae** contains fangless snakes, yet they are among the most dangerous animals.
answer:
> [!answer]
> Boas and pythons are **non-venomous** (no fangs) but kill by **constriction**: they coil around prey and squeeze until it suffocates or circulation stops. Large species can kill and swallow big animals.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Danger comes from size and strength, not venom.

## Simplified explanation

They **constrict** their prey.

body: Explain why the mode of reproduction of the Subclass **Theria** is better and safer than that of **Prototheria**.
answer:
> [!answer]
> Prototheria (monotremes) **lay eggs**, which are exposed to predators and temperature changes. Theria (marsupials and placentals) give birth to **live young**, with the embryo developing **inside the mother** (placentals via a placenta), protected, kept at constant temperature and nourished directly, so survival is higher.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Viviparity with internal development reduces mortality.

## Simplified explanation

Live birth protects the embryo; eggs are vulnerable.

body: (a) What is a **coelom**? (b) Give **four** functions of the coelom.
answer:
> [!answer]
> (a) A fluid-filled body cavity **completely lined by mesoderm**, between the gut and body wall.
>
> (b) Functions: (1) acts as a **hydrostatic skeleton**; (2) allows **organs to move and grow** independently of the body wall; (3) **cushions/protects** organs; (4) **transports** nutrients, wastes and gametes in the fluid; (5) provides space for organ development.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Animals are acoelomate (flatworms), pseudocoelomate (nematodes) or coelomate (annelids, molluscs, chordates).

## Simplified explanation

Mesoderm-lined cavity; skeleton, movement, protection, transport.

body: State **three** basic characteristics of chordates.
answer:
> [!answer]
> At some stage of life all chordates have: (1) a **notochord**; (2) a **dorsal hollow nerve cord**; (3) **pharyngeal slits/pouches**; (4) a **post-anal tail**.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

In vertebrates the notochord is replaced by the vertebral column.

## Simplified explanation

Notochord, dorsal nerve cord, pharyngeal slits, post-anal tail.

body: Describe **three** means by which you could break the **dormancy** of seeds.
answer:
> [!answer]
> 1. **Scarification**: scratching/nicking or acid treatment of a hard seed coat.
> 2. **Stratification**: exposure to cold (or warm then cold) moist conditions.
> 3. **Soaking/leaching** in water to remove germination inhibitors.
> 4. Treatment with **gibberellins**; exposure to **light**; heat/fire.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Dormancy may be due to an impermeable seed coat, inhibitors or an immature embryo.

## Simplified explanation

Scarify, stratify, soak, hormones.

body: Give **two** ecological importances of bryophytes.
answer:
> [!answer]
> 1. **Pioneer species**: colonise bare rock/soil and help **soil formation**.
> 2. **Prevent soil erosion** and retain water (e.g. *Sphagnum* mosses).
> 3. Provide **habitat** for small animals; act as **bio-indicators** of pollution.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Peat (from *Sphagnum*) is also used as fuel and in horticulture.

## Simplified explanation

Pioneers, soil, water, habitat.

body: State **three** strategies flowering plants adopt to be pollinated by animals.
answer:
> [!answer]
> 1. **Bright colours** and patterns (nectar guides, UV markings).
> 2. **Scent** (sweet for bees/moths; foul for flies).
> 3. **Rewards**: nectar and edible pollen.
> 4. Flower **shape/timing** suited to the pollinator (tubular for birds; night-opening for bats/moths).
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Co-evolution matches flowers to their pollinators.

## Simplified explanation

Colour, scent, nectar, shape.

body: List **three** reasons for the success of angiosperms.
answer:
> [!answer]
> 1. **Flowers** attract animal pollinators, making pollination efficient.
> 2. **Double fertilisation** gives an endosperm food store only when fertilisation occurs.
> 3. **Fruits** protect seeds and aid dispersal.
> 4. **Vessels** in the xylem conduct water efficiently.
> 5. **Short life cycles** and great adaptability to many habitats.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Angiosperms are the most diverse plant group.

## Simplified explanation

Flowers, double fertilisation, fruits, vessels.

body: Give **two** characteristics of **marsupials** and three examples.
answer:
> [!answer]
> Characteristics: young born **very immature** and complete development in a **pouch (marsupium)** attached to teats; no true (chorioallantoic) placenta.
>
> Examples: **kangaroo, koala, opossum** (wallaby, wombat).
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Marsupials are concentrated in Australia and the Americas.

## Simplified explanation

Pouch, immature young; kangaroo, koala, opossum.
